name: collection_id
description: Survey a delivered directory: classify every object in it (copied files, disk containers, memory captures, archives) from its first bytes and its name, and say which of the two each class rests on. A name that says image or raw with no signature behind it is unknown (a raw memory capture has none either), never a physical image; an 8 KiB boot sector, or a small nested file named like an image, is a copied file. The delivery is mixed when more than one kind of object is present (copied files below the top level count as one kind; a note or a log beside an image is another file, not a kind). It reads only the first 4 KiB of an object, never opens a container or lists an archive. Collectors are named by the paths of their records, more than one may be present and one may have run more than once; a top-level C, C$ or Windows directory is a layout clue that names no collector; a record found inside collected data ([root], uploads) belongs to the source host and is not read. Logs read whole and streamed: KAPE copy, skip and console logs (per run; columns and row counts, malformed rows located, each skip row kept whole with the collector's own words; console warnings and errors as rows of the problems table, not failures), UAC uac.log (lines that start with a date, a time and a level word, in the forms the sources of UAC 3.4.0, DBG INF ERR CMD, and 2.9.1, DEBUG INFO WARNING ERROR COMMAND, write; ERR and ERROR are failures, a command's stderr is counted apart, a line that matches nothing is counted and kept unlabelled, and a summary saying 0 errors is not a failure) and Velociraptor containers (checked against the source of 0.77.2, which writes no failed upload to uploads.json: the count comes from results/*.json upload records with an Error and the ERROR lines of log.json, so a container without them is partial). A log whose columns or lines are not recognised, or that is binary or UTF-16, is partial or unsupported; the rows of a skip log with unrecognised columns are kept whole in unrecognised_rows and are no failures. failed_target_count is null, never 0, unless every failure-source log was read whole, the walk was complete and no archive went unopened; failed_targets_seen is how many rows were read all the same. A recorded skip or error is the collector's own outcome, never explained or judged. Not measured: what the collector was asked to copy, that it finished, whether a digest matches the delivered file, source paths (collection_index), the collector's version, what a log omits. delivery.not_observed lists the kinds of object not seen among the files walked and says what qualifies it (an unknown object, an unopened archive, an incomplete walk): a limit of the delivery, no finding about the source. Paths and log text shaped like a recovery password, an access key, a token, a private-key block, URL user-info, or the value after a credential header, key name or password option are withheld (other secrets in a log can still appear: run it as a job with secret_output: true; the tool cannot see whether the job was run so); write_values: true (jobs only) writes the real strings to $OUT/collection-id-values.jsonl, mode 0600, created first, a second run in the same job refused. Every list is whole in a file the answer names (the problems table holds every walk error, link and log problem); the answer starts with the summary and ends with the pages. Every key and value of the answer and of the table files it names is withheld by shape, and the structure is then read back by a second check written apart from the first; a string that check finds suspect is replaced by <withheld: N bytes>, counted in the answer's boundary entry, and the answer is partial. Withholding is by shape. Measured on random plants (1,000 per shape and context: alone, in a path, a file name, a log line, a URL, an option, glued to letters), the 33 listed shapes (token prefixes, JWT, PEM, connection strings, user-info, name=value and option forms, recovery passwords), the unlisted token families (GitLab, Stripe, Google, npm, SendGrid, DigitalOcean, Twilio), names such as DB_PASSWORD= and adminPassword:, and tokens split by NUL, zero-width, bidi, UTF-16-in-8-bit or full-width characters or written in another case come out in 0.2% or fewer of the plants; AWS-secret-shaped keys and base64 of 20 to 48 bytes in 0.7% or fewer, base64 of 16 bytes in 2.5%, 20 random letters and digits in 1.5% and 32 in 0.5%; base36 text of 24 to 32 characters in 18% to 26%. A plain password or passphrase alone in a name, a UUID-shaped key, 24 lower-case letters and 16 characters of base32 are printed (100%). A secret of another shape is printed: a file whose secrets matter is read in a secret_output job. Cost on real names, measured: 0.47% of this repository's paths, 0.14% of 37,916 Linux package paths and 3.64% of 57,142 macOS system and application paths (hardware ids and GUID-named profiles read as random) are withheld.

root.description: The collection directory (an archive is not opened: extract it into a job's output first)

limit.description: Rows of each table shown inline (default 200); a longer table is whole in the file its *_table entry names

time_limit_seconds.description: Stop the walk and the log reads after this long (default 1500, at most 3400): the answer then says it stopped, status partial, and what was not listed

write_values.description: Write the real strings that were withheld to $OUT/collection-id-values.jsonl (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true; the file is created first and one already there is refused
